decisions.reason: The label-matching instruction does not change how placeholder text clears when a field is activated.
Requiring labels to match initial prompts does not change the requirement to preserve field formatting.
The source changes help-label content and coverage, not the visual mechanism used to identify fillable fields or its existing ambiguity.
The instruction about matching labels does not replace or modify the robust placeholder mechanism.
A checklist may be among the interactive fields covered by the label requirement, but its control type remains unchanged.
A dropdown may be among the interactive fields covered by the label requirement, but its control type and document scope remain unchanged.
The source does not alter the calendar-style date input method; label behavior is independently owned by the source Requirement.
The lexical match to 'match' and 'label' is incidental; the source does not address bullet appearance or formatting.
Interactive-field label content has no necessary effect on containment of pasted content within page margins.
The source does not change table paste stability, column boundaries, or the existing feasibility ambiguity.
The candidate was retrieved through historical mention of interactive-field labels, but the source does not modify the required theme colors.
Mentioning that the supplied version has been translated does not explicitly change the document-content or default-language configuration.
